definition: A short summary written for one reader, in which each statement links to the evidence behind it.
The operator's ability to tell, in the time she has, what the swarm did and why, and to check each statement against its evidence.
The property of a summary whose every statement opens, in one step, to the artifact behind it, such as the diff, the test log or the committed file.
A decision handed up to a human because no agent may make it alone.
A typed message whose declared type (request, commitment, delegation or termination) states what it intends, who owns it and when it ends.
A self-report that runs every invariant check, separates verified-good from no-evidence-of-bad, and fails loudly about what it cannot check.
A view that lists what the attention queue did not show the operator, and why.
An item's estimated harm if it is left unseen; in this chapter, stakes times irreversibility times anomaly.
Consent inferred from someone merely staying put, without any act of agreeing.
An explicit, scoped, time-limited and revocable authorization the operator gives the daemon, recording scope, stakes ceiling, minimum reversibility and expiry.
How much of a task a machine may do without asking a human, on Sheridan's ten-point scale.
Any view an operator or agent reads to learn the swarm's state, such as a briefing, a digest or the attention queue.
Hands-on, case-specific practical knowledge that a system depends on and that resists being written down (James C. Scott's term).
A digest whose lines assert a state nobody can check, because the evidence behind them was discarded.
Practitioner knowledge that cannot be fully put into words; in Polanyi's phrase, we know more than we can tell.
A versioned, amendable statement of intent, priority and dependency, organized by phase, against which the swarm's output is compared.
One named agent identity that alone may write the state a critical invariant protects.
A commitment whose satisfaction is decided by a verifier derived from the task's acceptance criteria.
In signal detection theory, how far apart the evidence scores of dangerous and safe items lie, written d′.
In signal detection theory, the threshold on the evidence score above which an item is inspected, written β.
Sustained watching for rare events.
The decline in detection that sets in over a long watch.
Perceiving the current state, understanding it, and projecting what happens next (Endsley's three levels).
The hypothesized slide by which an operator goes from doing the work, to approving it, to rubber-stamping it, to being absent.
A proposed, consented, blinded probe that slips known, already-fixed defects into review to measure whether the operator still catches them.
Shortening an agent's working context into a summary when the context runs out of room.
A regime in which legible state accumulates faster than anyone can read it, so participants search by eye or act blind.
A maintained list of which agents exist, what each says it can do, and where their records live.
The scoring function that ranks candidate agents for a query by a clamped weighted sum of file, note, identity, skill, episode and load signals.
One shared candidate list and decay rule with a separate scoring head for each reader, needed because collaborator fit and inspection priority can strictly disagree.
The change in expected settled outcome when a skill is made available to a task, compared with the same task without it.
The direct variable costs of producing output; for a swarm, chiefly inference tokens.
Multiplying every stored coordination trace by a decay factor each interval, so stale traces fade.
The root object of a many-author harbor, recording who delegated what to whom, which rule settles a clash, and how the charter itself may change.
The rule that each person reports to exactly one person; here, that every scope and every delegator has a single direct delegator.
The procedure that removes one principal's commitments at a time and reruns the conflict check, keeping each principal whose removal makes the conflict disappear.
The principals the deletion filter keeps: a group whose directions still conflict on their own, from which no one can be dropped.
